question: Can a mirror normal prior synthesized from multi-echo LiDAR (no labels, no GT) replace the GT mirror normal (gtnorm) on r300? Does first-echo LiDAR depth help on top?
data: normals data/datasets/mirror_b/r300_lidarnorm_open3 (mirror_lidar/tools/lidar_mirror_normals.py, 3x3 zone opening + see-through test; mirror normal err 0.016 deg, precision 99.95%, recall 96.9%, IoU 0.987); depth data/datasets/mirror_b/r300_lidar_depth (lidar_first_echo_depth.py, ~39k px/camera = 3.1%, median |err| 1.61 cm)
eval: data/logs/eval_r300_lidar.sh <run> <gpu> (eval_mirror_b_run.sh + flatness/normal_spread/per_obj), val 38 frames (26 with mirror)
conclusion: LiDAR-synthesized mirror normals match gtnorm_nw5 on every metric (mirror on plane 100%, depth std 4 mm, normal spread 0.60 vs 0.49 deg, PSNR 35.92 vs 35.84): the GT mirror normal can be replaced by the LiDAR fit. First-echo LiDAR depth (3% px, L1 0.1) fixes the remaining opaque geometry: opaque depth median 6.1 cm -> 0.3 cm, d<1.05 0.67 -> 0.99, ceiling 0.35 m -> 3 mm (the long-standing ceiling error), mirror std 2 mm, mirror PSNR +0.2, opaque PSNR -0.7 dB, total PSNR unchanged. Caveats: synthetic LiDAR has same-index frame/camera sync, exact extrinsics, mirror surface scatter 0.02.
